subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematical Methods, Units 3 and 4
syllabus: VCE Mathematics Study Design (from 2023), Mathematical Methods Units 3 and 4

points.title: Polynomial and power graphs in Unit 3
points.brief: Features of polynomial and power function graphs: intercepts, stationary points, inflections, asymptotes and domain.

points.title: Exponential and logarithmic graphs
points.brief: y = e^x and y = log_e(x) are inverses. Transformations move their asymptotes and intercepts.

points.title: Circular function graphs
points.brief: y = a sin(n(x − b)) + c and its cosine and tangent forms have amplitude, period, phase and centre set by a, n, b and c.

points.title: Transformations in mapping form
points.brief: A rule such as (x, y) → (2x + 1, 3y) describes dilations, reflections and translations together.

points.title: Sums and products of functions
points.brief: f + g and f × g are defined on the domain shared by both, and their graphs can be sketched by adding or multiplying heights.

points.title: Composite functions
points.brief: f(g(x)) applies g then f. It exists only when the range of g sits inside the domain of f.

points.title: Inverse functions in Unit 3
points.brief: A one-to-one function has an inverse whose domain is the function's range. Restricting a domain can make a function one-to-one.

points.title: Hybrid functions and modelling
points.brief: Piecewise (hybrid) functions and combinations of functions model real situations, such as a cost that changes rule above a threshold.

points.title: Polynomial equations in Unit 3
points.brief: A polynomial of degree n has at most n real solutions, found by factorising, by graph or numerically.

points.title: Exponential and logarithmic equations
points.brief: Solve by writing both sides with the same base or by taking logarithms, checking the domain of any log.

points.title: Trigonometric equations in Unit 3
points.brief: Find every solution in a domain using a reference angle, the quadrants and the period, including with transformations.

points.title: Literal and parameter equations
points.brief: Equations with a parameter, such as kx + 2 = 3, can have one, none or infinitely many solutions depending on k.

points.title: Systems of linear equations
points.brief: Simultaneous linear equations can have one solution, none or infinitely many, which a parameter can decide.

points.title: Numerical solutions
points.brief: When an equation cannot be solved exactly, numerical methods such as bisection find solutions to any accuracy.

points.title: Derivatives of exponential, log and circular functions
points.brief: The derivative of e^(kx) is k e^(kx), of log_e(x) is 1/x, of sin(kx) is k cos(kx) and of cos(kx) is −k sin(kx).

points.title: The chain rule
points.brief: The derivative of f(g(x)) is f′(g(x)) × g′(x).

points.title: The product rule
points.brief: The derivative of u × v is u′v + uv′.

points.title: The quotient rule
points.brief: The derivative of u/v is (u′v − uv′)/v².

points.title: Sketching derivative and antiderivative graphs
points.brief: The shape of a graph shows the shape of its derivative and of an antiderivative, without a rule.

points.title: Stationary points and curve sketching
points.brief: Derivatives find stationary points, points of inflection and where a function is strictly increasing or decreasing.

points.title: Optimisation
points.brief: Finding the largest or smallest value of a quantity in context, checking stationary points and the endpoints of the interval.

points.title: Rates of change in context
points.brief: The derivative gives the instantaneous rate of change of a quantity, such as velocity from position.

points.title: Antiderivatives in Unit 3
points.brief: Antiderivatives of x^n, e^(kx), 1/x, sin(kx) and cos(kx), each plus a constant.

points.title: Definite integrals
points.brief: A definite integral is the limit of a sum of thin strips, and has properties such as splitting across an interval.

points.title: The fundamental theorem of calculus
points.brief: Integration and differentiation undo each other, which links the area under a curve to antiderivatives.

points.title: Finding a function from its rate of change
points.brief: Antidifferentiating a rate and using a known point, a boundary condition, gives the function itself.

points.title: Area under and between curves
points.brief: Area is the integral of the top curve minus the bottom one, splitting where curves cross the axis or each other.

points.title: The trapezium rule
points.brief: Approximating area with trapeziums of equal width, which improves as the width shrinks.

points.title: Average value of a function
points.brief: The average value of f on [a, b] is the integral from a to b divided by b − a.

points.title: Random variables
points.brief: A random variable gives a number to each outcome of an experiment. It is discrete if it takes separate values and continuous if it takes any value in a range.

points.title: Discrete probability distributions
points.brief: A table or rule giving the probability of each value of a random variable, with the probabilities adding to 1.

points.title: Expected value and variance
points.brief: E(X) is the sum of x × Pr(X = x). Var(X) = E(X²) − (E(X))², and the standard deviation is its square root.

points.title: The binomial distribution
points.brief: The number of successes in n independent Bernoulli trials, each with the same chance p, has a binomial distribution.

points.title: Mean and variance of a binomial
points.brief: For a binomial, E(X) = np and Var(X) = np(1 − p).

points.title: Probability density functions
points.brief: A non-negative function whose total area is 1. Areas under it give probabilities for intervals.

points.title: Mean, median and variance of a continuous variable
points.brief: The mean is the integral of x f(x). The median splits the area in half.

points.title: The normal distribution
points.brief: A symmetric bell curve set by its mean μ and standard deviation σ.

points.title: The standard normal distribution
points.brief: Z = (X − μ)/σ turns any normal variable into one with mean 0 and standard deviation 1.

points.title: Populations and samples
points.brief: A sample statistic, such as a sample proportion, estimates a population parameter, and varies from sample to sample.

points.title: Simulating samples
points.brief: Repeated random samples, simulated with technology, show how a sample statistic varies from sample to sample.

points.title: The sample proportion
points.brief: The proportion of a sample with a feature varies between samples. For large samples its distribution is roughly normal.

points.title: Approximate confidence intervals
points.brief: A 95% confidence interval for p is p-hat ± 1.96 × √(p-hat(1 − p-hat)/n).

points.title: Interpreting a confidence interval
points.brief: About 95% of intervals made this way would contain the true proportion. Larger samples give narrower intervals.
